newsitem.title: USA: Some U.S. refiners show appetite for foreign crude.
newsitem.headline: Some U.S. refiners show appetite for foreign crude.

text.p: Some U.S. refiners began showing an appetite for foreign crude Thursday in response to the widening trans-Atlantic arbitrage, trade sources said.
The spread between January West Texas Intermediate and North Sea Brent was around $1.10-15 a barrel.
A Wall Street player sold one Brent VLCC for loading in late December to a Gulf Coast refiner at around February WTI plus 25 cents, trade sources said.
The firm has another Brent VLCC for loading around the same time which is still available, they said.
Most refiners continue to resist foreign crudes, however, in light of weakening prices for alternative domestic grades such as Light Louisiana Sweet/St.James.
LLS/St. James was trading around 68-72 cents premium to WTI/Cushing, down three to four cents from late Wednesday.

"Over the last several days, Gulf Coast refiners may be taking Brent. The spread is the primary reason, but it also depends on the price of domestic alternatives," a representative of a Gulf Coast refiner said.
Meanwhile, Iraqi crude is quickly making its way into the region under the oil-for-food deal brokered by the United Nations.

Coastal Corp was given clearance by the U.S. Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) for its deal to lift Iraqi crude. The firm is expected to take 60,000 barrels per day to its refinery on the Caribbean island of Aruba, sources said.
Texaco Inc said it is negotiating a separate deal with Iraq for 35,000-40,000 bpd.
Mobil is also in the running for a contract, sources said.

In Latin America, activity was subdued heading into the holidays. Chile's state oil company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (ENAP) received bids Thursday for its purchase tender for 960,000 barrels of crude for delivery January 28 to February 2.
In the U.S. aftermarket, a series of partial Brent cargoes changed hands at $22.58 and $22.60 a barrel, five to seven cents higher than the IPE settlement price.
Intermonth spreads were steady, with Jan/Feb Brent tradiing at 40 and 41 cents.
